newsitem.title: UK: S&P affirms Veba ratings, cuts outlook.
newsitem.headline: S&P affirms Veba ratings, cuts outlook.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Monday it had affirmed VEBA AG's senior unsecured AA plus rating and its A1 plus commercial paper rating.

S&P said it had changed its outlook to negative from stable, taking VEBA off CreditWatch, where it was placed with negative implications in May following the announcement of the acquisition of a 36.4 percent stake in the German public quoted company Degussa AG.

"The current rating category leaves only modest room for further mid-sized acquisitions spread over a medium term time horizon, in light of recent increased investment activity," S&P said in a statement.
It said the stability and predictability of VEBA's electricity business was expected to continue to underpin VEBA's creditworthiness.
S&P noted the company's electricity activities were organised under the management of the wholly owned PreussenElektra (PE) group.
S&P said said while the company's financial profile remained very strong, a stepped-up investment programme would modestly limit financial flexibility.

"Over time, the risk remains that VEBA's exposure to business with more volatile cash flow patterns, as well as the likely increase in PE's competitive environment, could also contribute to pressure being placed on current ratings," S&P said.
